subject: Hospitality
title: Acoustic Design in Restaurants
description: A fast breakdown of Acoustic Design in Restaurants for builders.

hook.text: A noisy restaurant forces guests to shout. A dead-silent one feels awkward. Acoustic design finds the sweet spot between the two.

buildup.text: Hard surfaces (glass, concrete, marble) reflect sound and create noise. Soft materials (fabric, carpet, acoustic panels) absorb.

discovery.text: Trendy industrial design—exposed brick, bare floors, metal ceilings—looks great but creates terrible acoustics.

twist.text: Some restaurants use 'pink noise'—a soft background hum—to fill silence without adding distraction.

climax.text: Acoustic Design in Restaurants matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: Too loud and guests leave early. Acoustics control how long people stay and spend.

quiz.question: What is 'pink noise' used for in restaurant design?
options: To fill silence with a soft background hum so quiet tables feel less exposed
